Definition: from G4012 and G71; to take around (as a companion); reflexively, to walk around:--compass, go (round) about, lead about.
BiblicalUsage: Periago means to lead about, to take around. Paul asks whether he has no power to lead about a sister, a wife, as the other apostles do, and Elymas went about seeking someone to lead him by the hand after Paul struck him blind.
TheologicalSignificance: What I believe is that leading about is a matter of whose hand holds mine: Paul's apostles led their wives, and the blinded sorcerer had to be led by a stranger.
